content.value_statement: Optimization projects often need repeatable algorithm selection, constraints, and Pareto front analysis. This skill guides pymoo workflows with examples, references, and troubleshooting patterns.
actual_capabilities: Selects pymoo algorithms for single, multi, and many-objective optimization problems.
Explains custom ElementwiseProblem definitions with bounds, objectives, and constraints.
Shows NSGA-II, NSGA-III, GA, SRES, and MCDM workflows.
Provides runnable example scripts for common optimization tasks.
Guides visualization choices for two, three, and many objectives.
Documents reference material for algorithms, operators, benchmarks, constraints, and visualization.
limitations: Does not install pymoo or dependencies automatically.
Does not prove mathematical correctness of user-defined objective functions.
Examples target pymoo 0.6.x APIs and may need updates for other versions.
Large optimization runs can be compute intensive and require careful termination settings.

use_cases.title: Compare Engineering Designs
use_cases.description: Find Pareto-optimal trade-offs across cost, weight, efficiency, or other competing design objectives.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Optimization Algorithms
use_cases.description: Run standard ZDT, DTLZ, or WFG problems to compare algorithm behavior and convergence.

use_cases.title: Tune Decision Models
use_cases.description: Normalize objective values and apply decision-making methods to choose preferred solutions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Algorithm
prompt_templates.prompt: I have one objective and continuous variables. Help me choose a pymoo algorithm, termination rule, and result checks.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Custom Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a constrained ElementwiseProblem for [domain]. Include objectives, bounds, constraints, and feasibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Pareto Front
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pymoo result summary. Recommend normalization, visualization, and MCDM methods for selecting a preferred solution.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Many-Objective Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an NSGA-III workflow for [number] objectives. Include reference directions, population settings, diagnostics, and convergence checks.

output_examples.input: Need a two-objective workflow for cost and weight minimization.
output: Recommended NSGA-II with a moderate population and generation-based termination.
Suggested scatter visualization for the Pareto front and optional pseudo-weight decision making.
Listed checks for objective scaling, duplicate solutions, and constraint feasibility.

output_examples.input: Need to create a constrained optimization problem for a process model.
output: Outlined decision variables, lower and upper bounds, objectives, and inequality constraints.
Recommended feasibility-first handling before penalty methods.
Included validation steps for constraint violations and result interpretation.

output_examples.input: Need to compare solutions across five objectives.
output: Recommended NSGA-III with reference directions suited to five objectives.
Suggested parallel coordinate plots and normalized objective values.
Provided decision-making options for selecting representative solutions.

best_practices: Normalize objectives when scales differ before comparing or applying decision methods.
Set random seeds and save history when results need reproducible analysis.
Choose termination rules that match runtime limits and convergence requirements.
anti_patterns: Using NSGA-III for simple two-objective problems without a reason.
Comparing objective values with different scales before normalization.
Ignoring constraint violation metrics when selecting final solutions.

faq.question: What is pymoo used for?
faq.answer: pymoo is used for optimization problems, especially multi-objective problems with Pareto front analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill run optimization jobs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and commands that users choose to run.

faq.question: Which algorithms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GA, DE, PSO, NSGA-II, NSGA-III, MOEA/D, SRES, and related methods.

faq.question: Can it help with constrained problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains feasibility-first handling, penalties, constraint-as-objective methods, and repair operators.

faq.question: Can it help select one solution from a Pareto front?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers normalization, pseudo-weights, compromise programming, knee points, and hypervolume contribution.

faq.question: What version is the guidance based on?
faq.answer: The skill states that its guidance is based on pymoo 0.6.x.
